prompt: Ana edited `hello/server.js` on the host and the container served the new text. What made that possible?
hint: Where did the file live, and what watched it?

choices.text: Docker rebuilt the image in the background
choices.why: Nothing was built; the stock image was used throughout.

choices.text: `docker cp` copied the file in on save
choices.why: No copy happened; the container read Ana's directory.

choices.text: A bind mount, and `node --watch`
choices.why: Right: the file was Ana's, and Node restarted on the change.

choices.text: Alpine reloads JavaScript
choices.why: The operating system does nothing of the kind.

prompt: Why does `compose.dev.yaml` give Go's build cache a named volume?
hint: What happens to a container's own files on restart and recreate?

choices.text: Go refuses to compile without a volume
choices.why: It compiles fine; it would just start from nothing each time.

choices.text: The cache volume also holds the database files
choices.why: There is no database in this file.

choices.text: To make the mounted source read-only for Go
choices.why: The source is the bind mount; the cache is separate.

choices.text: Restarts recompile only changes
choices.why: Right: the cache outlives any one container.

prompt: `shelf:dev` has `/src/shelf`, yet `docker run -v "$PWD/shelf":/src shelf:dev` says `./shelf: no such file`. Why?
hint: What does a mount do to what was there?

choices.text: Ana's directory replaces `/src` for that container
choices.why: Right: the image's binary is hidden behind it.

choices.text: The build failed silently
choices.why: Without the mount, `ls` found the binary.

choices.text: Bind mounts are read-only
choices.why: They are writable by default, and reading was the problem anyway.

choices.text: `CMD` needs an absolute path
choices.why: `./shelf` resolves against `WORKDIR`; the file was simply not there.

prompt: Which of these avoid the hidden-binary problem? Choose all that apply.
hint: Keep build output away from the mount.

choices.text: Build the binary into `/usr/local/bin`
choices.why: Yes: the mount on `/src` does not cover it.

choices.text: Run `go run` inside the container, as `compose.dev.yaml` does
choices.why: Yes: it builds after the mount is in place.

choices.text: Put the build output in a volume of its own
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: Mount the directory twice
choices.why: A second mount covers the first; nothing reappears.

prompt: Match each `develop.watch` action to what it does when a file changes.

pairs.right: Builds the image and recreates the service
Copies the file into the running container
Copies the file, then restarts the container

right_distractors: Pushes the image to a registry

prompt: What does `watch` with `rebuild` give that the bind-mounted `go run` setup does not?

choices.text: Faster feedback after each save, without a build
choices.why: It is slower: a full build each time.

choices.text: The image that ships, tested on every change
choices.why: Right: multi-stage, distroless and all.

choices.text: No need for a Dockerfile
choices.why: It builds from the Dockerfile.

choices.text: A debugger attached automatically to the new container
choices.why: Nothing attaches a debugger.

prompt: After the watch rebuilt the image, what was the `id` of the book `/books` returned at index 3?
Why does Node in the container listen with `--inspect=0.0.0.0:9229` rather than the default?

choices.text: The default port is reserved by Docker
choices.why: The port is the same; the address differs.

choices.text: So the debugger accepts connections from the internet
choices.why: The host side is still published on loopback only.

choices.text: A published port reaches `eth0`, not its loopback
choices.why: Right: the default `127.0.0.1` is the container's own.

choices.text: Node refuses to debug as a non-root user
choices.why: Users have nothing to do with it.

prompt: Why must a debugging port never be published on a network address?

choices.text: Debuggers use too much bandwidth on a shared network
choices.why: Bandwidth is not the risk.

choices.text: It slows the program
choices.why: Speed is not the risk either.

choices.text: Editors reject remote debuggers
choices.why: They accept them; that is the danger.

choices.text: Whoever reaches it runs code in the program
choices.why: Right: read any variable, run anything.

prompt: Node lists its debugging targets, with the WebSocket address an editor connects to, at `localhost:9229/json/___`.
A colleague adds `--inspect=0.0.0.0:9229` and `ports: ["9229:9229"]` to the production `compose.yaml` "for emergencies". What should Ana suggest?

choices.text: Move it to a development override, on `127.0.0.1`
choices.why: Right: development flags in a development file, on loopback.

choices.text: Keep it, but change the port number
choices.why: A different port is the same open debugger.

choices.text: Keep it, since `--inspect` is harmless in production
choices.why: It hands code execution to whoever reaches the port.

choices.text: Remove the healthcheck instead
choices.why: Unrelated, and the healthcheck is useful.
